aDefectThisLaneCaughtInItsOwnWork.defect: A TEST THAT PROVED NOTHING, caught by running it rather than by reading it.
aDefectThisLaneCaughtInItsOwnWork.howItShowedUp: The interpolation arm asserted `returnPeriodYearsForDepthInches(CURVE, 5.5).value === 10` exactly -- 5.5in IS a knot on the curve whose period is 10. It failed with 10.000000000000002. The log/exp round trip the client itself uses does not land on the integer.
aDefectThisLaneCaughtInItsOwnWork.theFix: Compared with a 1e-9 tolerance, AND the reason is written into the test: the rendered label rounds, so the screen is exact; asserting bit-equality would have been testing IEEE754 rather than the contract. The alternative fix -- snapping exact knots inside the function -- was REJECTED on purpose, because the design requires this interpolation to be the client's so the depth control and the engine's own PDF label can never disagree, and a local 'improvement' is exactly how two implementations of one rule start to drift.

whatIsMeasuredHere.theClient: Every refusal arm runs against a fetch that THROWS if it is called, so 'refuses before the network' is proven rather than asserted. The happy paths run against a canned fetch that records what it was asked, so the refresh-sends-depth / study-sends-none divergence is read off the request rather than inferred.

WHETHER THE DEPLOYED APP SETS HAUSKA_ENGINE_BASE. The client refuses cleanly without it, so this is a config question and not a code question, but it decides whether any of this can render a real study on bastrop_tx.
honestLimits: The engine client is proven against CANNED payloads that match the shapes read from the source at the pinned commit. It is NOT proven against a live engine response. A shape that differs in a field this module reads (rainfallSource, honestEmpty, stats) would be found only by the live probe.

The screening model has no test that drives a full multi-parcel list through the client; the list tests use hand-built determinations. That is a gap of integration coverage, not of unit coverage, and it closes with the route.
The depth presets are the design's own four (2, 4, 7, 10). The engine accepts any depth in (0, 60] and the basis text says so; nothing here constrains a caller to the presets.
No test asserts the SCREEN, because there is no screen. Every visual claim on the five artboards remains unbuilt and untested.
whatWouldFalsifyThisHalf: If a live engine study for bastrop_tx carries its shallow-water share under a key this module does not read, the screen will report 'unmeasured' for a parcel that ponds -- the field-name OPEN thread above, and the arm to read first.

If a live engine response omits rainfallSource on a study that WAS run at a passed depth, rainfallBasisLabel refuses rather than labels; that is deliberate, but it means the depth control's basis line can go blank on a payload the design expects to label.

If the engine's gate-context ever flips to enforce mode, these calls fail CLOSED into the honest engine_gate_config refusal -- by design, and it will look like a config fault rather than a code fault, which is why that class is named and not retryable.
